name: Kosta & Rinn Herringbone Pullover
description:
A mid-weight pullover sweater in a classic herringbone weave, cut slightly oversized with a ribbed crewneck and cuffs. The wool-analog fabric is dense enough to hold its shape through a workweek but soft enough to wear against bare skin. Available in four muted colorways: slate, bark, ash, and a deep burgundy called 'Korinthia.' The chest panel is subtly textured, giving it a handmade quality that the automated looms deliberately try to replicate.

Kosta & Rinn is a mid-tier label out of the Milwaukee corridor, family-operated for three generations, now producing out of a licensed micro-factory in Tier 3 residential. It sells in department stores and a few boutique shops. People who buy it tend to keep it for years.
what_it_says: You dress with intention without making it a statement. You probably own fewer clothes than most people but they're all good ones.
worn_by: people who grew up Tier 2 and made it to 3
story_hooks: A character finds one in their deceased parent's closet, still folded. It fits perfectly.
Kosta & Rinn is being quietly acquired by a corponation that plans to offshore production — the current run may be the last authentic batch.
Two strangers at a transit hub are wearing the same colorway and one of them takes it as a sign.

physical_description.visual_profile: A relaxed, substantial pullover with subtle texture and warmth. Sits slightly oversized on the frame, creating a comfortable, lived-in silhouette that reads as intentional rather than sloppy. The herringbone weave catches light differently depending on angle, giving the garment quiet visual depth.
physical_description.fit: Slightly oversized through the chest and shoulders; straight cut through the torso with gentle tapering at the sides. Ribbed crewneck sits at natural collarbone. Sleeves hit mid-forearm with snug ribbed cuffs. Designed for layering or standalone wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-analog synth-blend; dense, durable weave that mimics natural fiber properties without moisture sensitivity. Micro-factory processed for consistent quality at Tier 3 price point.
physical_description.texture: Herringbone diagonal weave creates subtle tactile variation. Chest panel deliberately textured to suggest handcraft—micro-irregularities in the knit that feel organic despite machine production. Soft against skin; slightly napped surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Four muted, naturalistic colorways: slate (cool gray-blue), bark (warm brown), ash (neutral taupe), and Korinthia (deep burgundy with slight plum undertone). All desaturated, professional palette.
physical_description.closures: None—pullover construction. No visible fasteners, zips, or snaps.
distinctive_features: Deliberately imperfect chest panel texture suggesting artisanal quality
Ribbed crewneck and cuffs in matching material
Subtle internal care tag with Kosta & Rinn Milwaukee corridor branding
Reinforced shoulder seams and cuff edges for durability
No logo or visible branding on exterior
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 — aspirational quality at working-class price. Signals stability and taste without wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Milwaukee-corridor workers, small business owners, and mid-tier office staff who value durability and quiet aesthetics. Appeals to people who reject fast-fashion cycles and corpo excess. Signals independent, locally-conscious values.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in beautifully. Starts crisp and textured; softens with wear while maintaining shape. After years, develops gentle fading and slight pilling on high-friction areas (underarms, cuffs), which owners typically embrace as patina rather than flaw.
